reasons: Deviation call is sound: the original clause bars any Customer convenience exit during the 12-month Initial Term of an auto-renewing agreement and gives Kubient a symmetrical 'for any reason' 90-day right exercisable at any time after the Initial Term, rather than only at end of term — short of the preferred position and of the fallback's vendor-side limit.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it inserts a Customer 30-day convenience right (including during the Initial Term) with refund of prepaid fees and an express no-early-termination-fee statement, and confines Kubient's convenience right to the end of the then-current Term on not less than 90 days' notice. Only the two offending sentences were replaced; the material-breach and insolvency provisions are untouched.

The 0.736 changed-character ratio is explained by the required replacement of the 'Neither Party may terminate during the Initial Term' and symmetrical 'either Party ... for any reason' sentences; no gratuitous rewriting of surrounding text.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, states what changed and why, and offers the 60–90 day fallback as the playbook contemplates.

Minor residual (not fatal): the retained sentence entitling Kubient to 'all fees generated during the termination period' sits alongside the new prepaid-fee refund; a follow-up tweak clarifying that this applies only to fees accrued through the effective date of termination would remove any ambiguity.
